newsitem.title: USA: Tonya Harding says she escapes bizarre kidnapping.
newsitem.headline: Tonya Harding says she escapes bizarre kidnapping.

text.p: Figure skater Tonya Harding told police she was kidnapped and forced to drive about 30 miles (48 km) early on Wednesday but escaped by ramming her pickup truck into a tree, authorities said.

Clackamas County Deputy Sheriff Damon Coates said authorities were investigating Harding's report that she was kidnapped by a man in his late 20s or early 30s outside her home near the Portland suburb of Milwaukie.
Harding, 26, told police she had gone outside to get cigarettes from her truck when she discovered the man tampering under the hood of another vehicle in her driveway, Coates said.
The man allegedly pulled a knife and said, "Get your car keys, you're going to take me where I need to go," Coates said.
The suspect, described as a white man with dark shaggy hair and a moustache, gave no indication that he knew who Harding was and or what his motive was.

With the man holding the knife to her cheek, Harding drove south for about half an hour until the man ordered her to pull over. She then decided to try to escape by ramming the truck into a tree and fleeing into the woods, Coates said.
Harding managed to hide behind a bush, and when the kidnapper ran past her she ran back to the truck, which still had the keys in it, and drove away.
Harding used her cell phone to call her boyfriend, who called police, Coates said.

Harding could not provide a detailed description of her attacker, saying he had ordered her to keep her eyes on the road for most of their journey. However, she was able to show police the route she took, including the tree she rammed.
And Harding had a red mark on her cheek where the man allegedly slapped her with the back of his hand.
"There are definitely some things to substantiate what she's saying," Coates said.

Harding was sentenced to 500 hours of community service and fined $160,000 in 1994 after admitting she covered up what she knew about an attack by her associates on rival U.S. Olympic skater Nancy Kerrigan.
The U.S. Figure Skating Association banned Harding from competition, but she has made periodic attempts at a comeback.

In the latest such effort, titled "Tonya II: The Comeback Campaign," Harding is scheduled to skate an exhibition before a sold-out minor-league hockey game Feb. 22 in Reno, Nev., her agent, David Hans Schmidt, said.
He said Harding had suffered only minor lacerations and was prepared for the exhibition.
